audit_scope.description: Trust model for EIP-7045 (Attestation Inclusion Window Extension), Cancun MODEXP precompile, EIP-6789 (Gas to Mana renaming), Cancun ecrecover precompile, and Cancun VM jump destination validation. Covers CL attestation mechanics, cryptographic precompile security, RPC interface changes, ECDSA recovery, and EVM control flow security.

in_scope: MODEXP precompile input parsing and gas calculation
MODEXP computation and edge case handling
ecrecover precompile signature recovery and validation
EVM jump destination validation (Cancun VM runtime)
Control flow security via JUMPDEST validation
RPC endpoint interface changes (EIP-6789 mana renaming)
EVM opcode execution with mana terminology
out_of_scope: Smart contract language bindings (Solidity/Vyper mana changes)

misclassified_entities.reason: Contract Calling MODEXP is an internal EVM component - contracts invoke precompiles via CALL opcode within the execution environment
Calling Contract for ecrecover is an internal EVM component - smart contracts invoking ecrecover for signature verification are part of internal EVM execution

trusted_external_entities.name: Attesting Validator
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Attestation creation for beacon chain slots
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Validators have 32 ETH staked and are economically incentivized. The extended inclusion window (until last slot of epoch N+1) allows more attestations to be included, improving LMD-GHOST security. Validators are semi-trusted due to stake but can still misbehave.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Proposer
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Beacon block construction with attestation inclusion
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Block proposers include attestations within the extended window. They are economically incentivized via staking but could selectively exclude attestations. Proposers must validate attestation eligibility before inclusion.

trusted_external_entities.name: Network Peer
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Network peers propagating attestations are untrusted. Attestation validation must check minimum slot requirement and target epoch (current or previous) before accepting attestations from peers.

trusted_external_entities.name: Gossip Network Peer
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P gossip channel for attestations and aggregates
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Gossip peers can attempt to propagate stale or invalid attestations. The extended gossip window conditions must be verified before propagation. Attestations outside the extended window must be dropped.

trusted_external_entities.name: RPC Client
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External RPC clients calling renamed mana endpoints are untrusted. The underlying computation is identical to former gas endpoints. Input validation and rate limiting apply as before.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Attestation creation and extended inclusion window
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Attestations are valid for inclusion from creation slot until the last slot of epoch N+1. The TIMELY_TARGET_FLAG is set without inclusion_delay constraint, guaranteeing non-zero reward for all valid attestations within the extended window.
Attestation validation must verify minimum slot requirement and target epoch (current or previous). The upper-bound slot check is removed in favor of epoch-based validation.
Extended gossip conditions must be checked before propagation. Stale attestations outside the extended window must be dropped without forwarding to prevent network pollution.
Renamed endpoints have identical security properties to former gas endpoints. The renaming is purely semantic and does not change validation, rate limiting, or computation logic.

coverage_gaps: MODEXP and ecrecover precompile external entities (EXT-CONTRACT-CALLER, EXT-CALLING-CONTRACT) are misclassified internal EVM components - the actual external boundary is at the transaction submission level covered by other batches
Cancun VM jump destination validation has no external entities - it is an internal EVM security mechanism operating on already-loaded bytecode
EXT-BLOCK-PROPOSER-EIP7045 acts at the CL level for attestation inclusion, not directly at EL interfaces
